claim_ceiling: RRVR supplies supporting execution and recovery evidence only; it does not establish standards compliance, a safety function, PL, SIL, safe state, certification or physical robot safety.

standards.scope: Machinery hazard identification, risk estimation/evaluation and risk reduction.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Failure-mode scoping, system boundary and operating assumptions.
standards.claim_limit: RRVR does not perform or replace the deployment risk assessment.

standards.scope: Industrial robot as an incomplete machine; inherent safe design and information for use.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Robot/endpoint identity, design assumptions and operating envelope.
standards.claim_limit: Industrial robot scope only; not a universal service/mobile robot standard.

standards.scope: Industrial robot application/cell integration, commissioning, operation, maintenance and decommissioning.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Integrator-level lifecycle, configuration and recovery evidence.
standards.claim_limit: Check explicit scope limitations, including mobile-platform and public-access cases.

standards.scope: Design and integration methodology for safety-related parts of control systems, including software, in high-demand/continuous modes.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Evidence lineage can support review of control-system verification artefacts.
standards.claim_limit: RRVR does not calculate or establish PL, category, PFHd, MTTFd or DC.

standards.scope: Design, integration and validation of machinery safety-related control systems.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Link RRVR execution/recovery claims to the actual safety-related control-system lifecycle.
standards.claim_limit: Does not replace risk assessment or security-specific controls.

standards.scope: Functional safety of electrical/electronic/programmable electronic safety-related systems.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Monitor edition changes affecting lifecycle, AI, security and independence expectations.
standards.claim_limit: Do not treat PRV as final published edition without checking IEC lifecycle record.

standards.scope: Safety requirements and verification for driverless industrial trucks and their systems, including specified AGV/AMR categories.
standards.rrvr_relevance: AMR execution, safety and system-level integration evidence within the standard scope.
standards.claim_limit: Use published 2023 edition until ISO/DIS 3691-4 is published; check operating environment exclusions.

standards.scope: Technical security requirements for industrial automation/control-system components.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Device identity, system integrity, restricted data flow, timely response and availability threat coverage.
standards.claim_limit: Component capability requirements do not establish deployment target/achieved security level.

standards.scope: Historical guidance on security threats/vulnerabilities that can undermine functional safety of machinery control systems.
standards.claim_limit: IEC catalogue marks it replaced; identify applicable successor before formal use.

standards.scope: Hardware/controller lifecycle and command interface behavior for the Lyrical release.
standards.rrvr_relevance: Exact plugin/driver-specific stale-command and lifecycle assay.
standards.claim_limit: Not a functional-safety standard; previously received command-value handling is implementation-dependent.

evidence_owners.supports: Intent-before-mutation and restart safety properties in the checked abstraction.
evidence_owners.does_not_support: Storage/power-loss durability or physical effect truth.

evidence_owners.supports: Reservation and replay properties in the checked concurrent ledger abstraction.
evidence_owners.does_not_support: Atomicity between a real remote ledger and physical actuator.

evidence_owners.supports: One-shot token and authority-epoch model properties.
evidence_owners.does_not_support: Firmware implementation, NVM anti-rollback or physical effect cardinality.

evidence_owners.supports: Intent-before-mutator ordering and restart suppression in the adapter.
evidence_owners.does_not_support: Live ROS/Gazebo, remote injector, HIL or physical behavior.

evidence_owners.supports: Structural consistency of declared command graph and supplied per-layer receipts.
evidence_owners.does_not_support: Inventory completeness or hardware quiescence without platform receipts.

evidence_owners.supports: Observer dependency analysis relative to declared fault models.
Scoped closed-cut decision under supplied graph/bounds and formal abstraction.
evidence_owners.does_not_support: Real transport bounds, endpoint expiry, physical NoEffect or certification.

evidence_owners.supports: Fresh attempt admission remains with existing authority owner.
evidence_owners.does_not_support: Safety function adequacy or device behavior.
